notes.text: This is a continuation leaf without an author page number at its head. It has sixteen main text/display rows, two diagonal left-margin paragraphs, a cancelled circled item number before the lower paragraph, two raised replacements/insertions, and thin foliation 18 at the bottom left. The lower remainder is blank. The whole original and both supplied native halves were inspected once each. Seventeen saved crops were inspected once each: P16 completes unresolved right endpoints clipped in P08/P09, and root-requested P17 completes the ascenders and attachment leader of the mandatory insertion clipped by P11. These completion views do not repeat decided targets. All boxes use original 1682×2359 coordinates; P08/P09/P16 are rotated clockwise45 for reading. H’s page-order note, marginal-reading commentary and final editorial note are not source text.

The opening continuation speaks of local triviality of the family of dotted T_i within dotted T over Y, after cancelling globalement. It extends equisingularity to an ambient pair X,(X_i) by using a cone neighborhood T of Y and the family X_i intersect T. The connectedness sentence has an explicit premise that each X_i intersect Y is open and closed in Y, followed by alternative (14). The first marginal note defines strict equisingularity by additional strict compatibility with every X_i; compatible itself remains paleographically doubtful. The second margin and the end of the lower paragraph assert strictness for each scaled lambda T with 0<lambda<1. The lower paragraph adds (globalement) before equisingulier le long de Y. This note describes source claims; the proof and counterexample scopes are given separately.

Independent proof of (14) under the written clopen premise and the cone-action stability required by compatibility. Fix i and put A_i=X_i intersect Y. If Y is connected and A_i is both open and closed in Y, then A_i is empty or Y. If A_i=Y, the second alternative X_i superset Y holds. If A_i is empty and x belonged to X_i intersect T, stability under the zero scalar would put 0·x in X_i intersect T; the cone action sends 0·x into Y, contradicting A_i empty. Hence X_i intersect T is empty, giving the first alternative. The argument is pointwise in i and needs no finiteness of the family. Local triviality is unnecessary for this implication once the clopen premise and zero-action stability are supplied. It does not by itself prove that local triviality implies that premise.

Counterexample proposed by the root and independently verified here against the intrinsic-cone plus ambient-neighborhood interpretation supplied for this run. Let q=3/8, H=[0,1]×{0}, V={q}×[0,1], and X=H union V with its Euclidean subspace topology. Set Y={(0,0)} and T=[0,1/2]×{0}. T is a closed cone and an ambient neighborhood of Y, since it contains an open initial horizontal segment; the scalar action is mu·(t,0)=(mu t,0). Its specified outer boundary is dotted T={(1/2,0)}, so the map dotted T→Y is globally trivial. Take the family with its sole member X_1=X; the boundary family and compatibility requirement are then trivial. For lambda=3/4, the scaled cone is S=lambda T=[0,q]×{0}, its boundary is p=(q,0), and its intrinsic interior is [0,q)×{0}. The exterior X minus that intrinsic interior consists of the right horizontal branch [q,1]×{0} and the vertical branch {q}×[0,1], meeting only at p. Removing p separates this exterior into two nonempty open-and-closed components. Every neighborhood of p meets both components. If a cylindrical neighborhood of the singleton boundary existed, it would be homeomorphic as a pair to ({p}×[0,1],{p}×{0}); after deleting p its image would be connected, yet would meet both separated components. This is impossible. Thus S has no point collar in its exterior and fails strictness in the exterior-collar sense required by strict compatibility. This refutes the universal assertion N04.L that every lambda T, 0<lambda<1, is strict under those literal assumptions. A stronger standing requirement that the intrinsic interior be open in X, or an ambient collar condition at every radial level, would exclude this branched example; such a strengthened assertion is not what this counterexample refutes.

Scope check on the preceding counterexample. The same example does not refute existence of a sufficiently small strict equisingular cone neighborhood. For any radial endpoint r=lambda/2 different from q, choose delta>0 small enough that the horizontal interval [r,r+delta] avoids the branch point q and lies in [0,1]. It is a neighborhood of r in the corresponding exterior, and s↦(r+delta s,0) identifies it with a point collar. In particular every 0<lambda<3/4 has such a collar, and the original endpoint r=1/2 does as well. With X_1=X the collar-compatibility condition is automatic. The specific failure is the universal quantifier over all rescalings of a given T, including the critical lambda=3/4. H’s phrase “ce qui équivaut à ce que” is not written: the manuscript says “auquel cas”, so no extra equivalence is introduced into the transcription.

Literal notation diagnostic, separate from the collar counterexample. The final neighborhood premise reads “un voisinage cônique” followed by cancelled doubtful de and live dotted T “de Y dans X”. The upper point is physically separate and uncancelled. For the standard mapping-cylinder cone C(f) with outer boundary represented by B×{1} and base Y obtained from B×{0}, that outer boundary is disjoint from Y. If Y is nonempty, dotted T alone therefore cannot contain Y and cannot be a neighborhood of Y. Undotted T is the mathematically plausible intended object, but the transcript preserves the dotted form. N04 evaluates the intended cone-neighborhood assertion with T as the ambient cone, rather than treating this visible source slip as a new definition.

Reading diagnostics. Ordinary T roofs are not added bars; the first dotted T_i, the T in (14), and the lower dotted T have substantial body or roof overwork without a recoverable prior glyph. The tiny point after the first T in the P04 parenthesis is retained explicitly after root inspection, with a T_i alternative. Its mathematical role remains unassigned; the earlier dismissal as a pen remnant is withdrawn. The darker group below main implique is the live à in the diagonal note, not a separate cancelled main word. The insertion leader of (globalement) is not an underline of équisingulier le long de Y. Both written cônique occurrences have a separate arch over o. The main grammar “on dit / il est” is left as written, without supplying qu’. The open intervals, source phi, underlined ou and written equals-sign shorthand are retained exactly.

Independent audit: root inspected all 14 nonidentical boxes, the completed diagonal-note crop and a wider native context separating marginal strokes from main prose. Four boxes were revised. The detached point in the family formula is now transcribed with an index alternative; three other revisions add local uncertainty without changing their preferred readings. The immutable first/second readings are preserved.
